title: Analyze Customer Journey Funnel Drop-offs via Tableau
t1: Establish a live connection between Tableau Desktop and AEP Query Service by entering the host, port, database, and PostgreSQL credentials found in the Platform UI under Query Service settings.
t2: Author a SQL query in Tableau's custom SQL dialog to extract step-by-step funnel progression events from the ExperienceEvent dataset, grouping records by journey stage and drop-off point.
t3: Build a funnel chart visualization in Tableau that illustrates conversion rates and drop-off percentages at each customer journey stage, enabling stakeholders to identify and prioritize optimization opportunities.

title: Profile Attribute Distribution Reporting in Tableau
t1: Connect Tableau to AEP Query Service using the SSL-enabled PostgreSQL connection details available in the Platform UI, ensuring secure access to the unified profile datasets.
t2: Write a SQL query within Tableau to aggregate Real-Time Customer Profile attributes—such as age bands, geographic regions, and loyalty tiers—across the profile store dataset to compute distribution counts.
t3: Design a set of interactive bar and map charts in Tableau that display the demographic and geographic distribution of customer profiles, allowing business analysts to filter and drill down by specific attributes.

title: Dataset Ingestion Quality Monitoring Dashboard in Tableau
t1: Set up a Tableau connection to AEP Query Service by configuring a named data source using the PostgreSQL JDBC driver and the credentials exported from the Platform UI's Query Service credentials panel.
t2: Compose a SQL query in Tableau targeting the AEP system datasets to retrieve batch ingestion metrics—including record counts, error rates, and ingestion timestamps—grouped by source connector and date.
t3: Construct a monitoring dashboard in Tableau featuring time-series trend lines and error-rate heat maps that give data engineers a real-time view of dataset ingestion health and allow alerting on anomaly thresholds.

title: Subscribe to destination dataflow failure alert
t1: Navigate to the Alerts section in Experience Platform and browse the list of available alert types related to destinations and dataflows.
t2: Select the destination dataflow run failure alert and subscribe to it using your preferred notification channel, such as email or in-platform notification.
t3: Receive an immediate alert when a destination dataflow run fails, allowing you to quickly diagnose the issue and re-run or troubleshoot the affected dataflow.

title: Subscribe to source dataflow ingestion delay alert
t1: Open the Alerts section within Experience Platform and filter the available alert catalog to locate alerts related to source connectors and data ingestion.
t2: Select the source dataflow ingestion delay alert and enable it by subscribing with your email address or configuring an in-platform notification preference.
t3: Receive a timely notification whenever a source dataflow exceeds its expected ingestion window, enabling you to investigate upstream data pipeline issues before they impact downstream processes.

title: Subscribe to identity graph capacity limit alert
t1: Navigate to the Alerts section in Experience Platform and search the alert catalog for alerts related to Identity Service and identity graph usage thresholds.
t2: Select the identity graph capacity limit alert and subscribe to it, choosing your preferred notification method to ensure you are informed when usage approaches the defined limit.
t3: Receive an alert when your identity graph nears its capacity threshold, prompting you to review identity settings and take corrective action to prevent data loss or graph collapse.

title: Re-engage cart abandoners with a personalized email discount offer
t1: Capture a cart abandonment event using AEP streaming ingestion when a customer leaves the site without purchasing, and store the abandoned cart product details in their Real-Time Customer Profile.
t2: Use Journey Optimizer to evaluate a wait condition of 2 hours after the cart abandonment event, then qualify the customer into a targeted email journey segment if no purchase has been completed.
t3: Deliver a personalized email via Journey Optimizer using Dynamic Content blocks that display the exact abandoned products alongside a time-limited discount code to incentivize purchase completion.

title: Suppress cart abandonment messaging for customers who complete purchase
t1: Ingest both cart abandonment and purchase completion events into AEP in real time, updating the customer's unified profile with the latest interaction state to reflect whether a purchase has occurred.
t2: Configure a Journey Optimizer journey with a business rule that checks the customer's profile for a subsequent purchase event during a defined suppression window, and exit the customer from the journey if a purchase is detected.
t3: For customers who remain in the journey without completing a purchase, send an SMS message via Journey Optimizer's SMS channel action reminding them of their cart items and providing a direct checkout link.

title: Orchestrate a multi-step cart abandonment retargeting sequence
t1: Define an AEP audience using Segment Builder that identifies customers who triggered an add-to-cart event but have no corresponding purchase event within a 24-hour lookback window, and schedule the audience to refresh every hour.
t2: Activate the cart abandonment audience into Journey Optimizer using an Audience Read activity, enrolling qualifying customers into a multi-step journey that enforces frequency capping and channel fatigue rules.
t3: Execute a sequential messaging flow within Journey Optimizer that first sends an in-app notification when the customer next opens the app, and if unopened after 12 hours, escalates to a push notification with a personalized product recommendation drawn from the abandoned cart data.

title: Build real-time customer segments using streaming data
t1: Ingest real-time behavioral event data into Adobe Experience Platform by configuring a streaming source connector and mapping the incoming fields to an XDM schema.
t2: Create a streaming segment definition in the Segmentation Service by specifying event-based rules that evaluate profile membership in real time as new data arrives.
t3: Activate the streaming segment to a downstream destination, such as Adobe Target, to deliver personalized experiences to qualifying customers within milliseconds of qualification.

title: Orchestrate a post-purchase email nurture journey in Journey Optimizer
t1: Define a purchase completion event in Adobe Journey Optimizer by mapping the relevant XDM Experience Event fields so the system can listen for and trigger on confirmed order data.
t2: Build a multi-step Journey canvas that begins with the purchase event trigger, adds wait nodes for timed delays, and inserts email action nodes configured with personalized post-purchase content.
t3: Publish the Journey and monitor its live execution through the Journey Optimizer reporting dashboard to track open rates, click-through rates, and journey completion metrics.

title: Centralize customer identity resolution across devices using Identity Service
t1: Configure an identity namespace in Adobe Experience Platform Identity Service to represent each identifier type, such as email, CRM ID, or mobile advertising ID, used across your data sources.
t2: Ingest customer records from multiple channels into Platform and ensure each dataset includes the appropriate identity fields so that Identity Service can stitch records into a unified identity graph.
t3: Validate the resulting identity graph in the Profile viewer to confirm that cross-device and cross-channel identities are correctly merged into a single customer profile before activating to downstream applications.

title: Resolve a stalled batch ingestion dataflow
t1: Navigate to the Sources monitoring dashboard and identify a dataflow stuck in a 'Processing' state beyond its expected completion window.
t2: Drill into the stalled batch run details to examine the ingestion logs and determine that an oversized file is exceeding the platform's batch size limits.
t3: Split the oversized source file into smaller compliant chunks, re-upload them to the source storage, and trigger a new dataflow run to verify all batches ingest successfully.

title: Diagnose and fix a broken streaming dataflow connection
t1: Open the Dataflows monitoring view in AEP and locate a streaming dataflow showing a sustained drop to zero records ingested over the past hour.
t2: Inspect the dataflow's connection status and error details to confirm the source HTTP streaming endpoint credentials have expired, causing authentication failures.
t3: Update the streaming source connector with refreshed API credentials, save the configuration, and monitor the dataflow metrics to confirm record throughput is restored.

title: Investigate and remediate a dataset ingestion backlog
t1: Review the Sources monitoring dashboard and detect an unusually large queue of pending batches accumulating in a scheduled dataflow over several consecutive runs.
t2: Examine the dataflow run metrics and system alerts to identify that a downstream dataset schema change introduced an incompatible field type, causing batches to queue without processing.
t3: Revert the dataset schema field to its original compatible type in Schema Editor, clear the pending batch queue, and re-enable the dataflow schedule to confirm the backlog processes without errors.

title: Analyze journey drop-off rates in a stakeholder report
t1: Open Customer Journey Analytics and build a fallout visualization to identify the specific steps where users are dropping off within your defined customer journey.
t2: Review the fallout report to pinpoint the highest drop-off stages, using segment comparisons to understand which audience cohorts are most affected.
t3: Export the finalized fallout visualization and supporting metrics as a PDF report to share with marketing stakeholders for review and action planning.

title: Evaluate email campaign KPIs using Journey Optimizer reporting
t1: Navigate to the Adobe Journey Optimizer Reports section and open the campaign-level report for your most recent email campaign to load delivery and engagement metrics.
t2: Examine key performance indicators including open rates, click-through rates, bounces, and unsubscribes to assess overall campaign health and audience responsiveness.
t3: Export the campaign performance summary from Journey Optimizer and share it with the marketing team via a scheduled report or direct download for post-campaign debriefs.

title: Review real-time segment audience trends for quarterly planning
t1: In Adobe Experience Platform, navigate to the Audiences section and select a key segment to open its detailed profile, reviewing membership trends and real-time qualification data over the past quarter.
t2: Cross-reference the audience growth or decline trends against campaign activation dates using the segment timeline to correlate marketing efforts with changes in segment size.
t3: Capture the audience trend charts and membership statistics by exporting the segment summary, then incorporate the data into a quarterly performance presentation for leadership review.

title: Web behavioral event schema setup
t1: Create an XDM ExperienceEvent schema and add the Web Details field group to capture page view URLs, referrer information, and session data from web interactions.
t2: Add the End User ID Details field group and designate the ECID (Experience Cloud ID) as the primary identity to enable cross-device visitor recognition.
t3: Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile and set the appropriate data retention policy so web behavioral events are unified with existing customer records.

title: CRM contact record schema setup
t1: Create an XDM Individual Profile schema and add the Personal Contact Details and Demographic Details field groups to capture customer name, email, phone, and date of birth.
t2: Add a custom field group to include CRM-specific attributes such as account tier, assigned sales representative, and contract start date, then define the CRM customer ID as the primary identity.
t3: Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so that CRM contact records can be ingested and merged into unified customer profiles for downstream segmentation.

title: Mobile app interaction event schema setup
t1: Create an XDM ExperienceEvent schema and add the Mobile Lifecycle Details and Application Details field groups to capture app launch events, screen views, and crash reports from mobile sessions.
t2: Add the IdentityMap field group and configure the hashed email address and device advertising ID as identity fields to associate mobile events with known customer profiles.
t3: Enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile and tag it with the appropriate data usage labels to ensure mobile interaction events comply with data governance policies before streaming ingestion begins.

title: Label loyalty ID as primary identity in event schema
t1: Open your ExperienceEvent schema in the Schema Editor and navigate to the field group containing the loyalty membership ID field you want to use as the primary identity.
t2: Mark the loyalty ID field as an identity field, set it as the primary identity, and assign it to a custom loyalty namespace you have previously created in Identity Service.
t3: Save the schema and enable it for Real-Time Customer Profile so that incoming event data uses the loyalty ID as the primary key for linking events to unified customer profiles.

title: Create and assign a custom namespace for partner IDs in a B2B schema
t1: Navigate to Identity Service in the AEP UI and create a new custom identity namespace for your partner-supplied customer IDs, specifying the identity type as Cross-Device.
t2: Open the target B2B account schema in the Schema Editor, select the partner ID field, and assign it the newly created custom namespace to designate it as an identity field.
t3: Enable the updated B2B schema for Real-Time Customer Profile so that records ingested with the partner ID are resolved and stitched across data sources using the identity graph.

title: Label ECID and IDFA fields in a mobile app event schema
t1: Open the mobile ExperienceEvent schema in the Schema Editor and locate the ECID and IDFA fields within the Identity Map or a custom field group added for device identifiers.
t2: Mark the ECID field as the primary identity using the standard ECID namespace, then mark the IDFA field as a secondary identity using the standard IDFA namespace to support cross-device identity resolution.
t3: Save the schema changes and confirm the schema is enabled for Real-Time Customer Profile, ensuring that mobile event data ingested via the Mobile SDK will correctly populate the identity graph with both identifiers.

title: Ingest CRM contact data into unified customer profiles
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
t1: Create an XDM Individual Profile schema for CRM contact data, defining fields such as email, phone, and customer ID, and enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile.
t2: Set up a source connector for your CRM platform (e.g., Salesforce) in AEP and map the CRM contact fields to the XDM schema to initiate data ingestion into a new dataset.
t3: Enable the resulting CRM contact dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile, ensuring ingested CRM records are merged into unified profiles using the defined identity namespace.

title: Stream website behavioral events into Real-Time Customer Profile
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
t1: Create an XDM ExperienceEvent schema capturing website behavioral events such as page views and product clicks, and enable the schema for Real-Time Customer Profile with a primary identity field.
t2: Configure a Web SDK datastream in AEP Data Collection to route real-time website event data to AEP, associating it with the XDM ExperienceEvent schema and a streaming inlet.
t3: Verify that the streaming dataset receiving website events is enabled for Real-Time Customer Profile, so behavioral event data is continuously appended to unified customer profiles in real time.

title: Bring offline purchase records into unified profiles via batch ingestion
source: Real-Time Customer Profile / Bring data into profile
t1: Define an XDM ExperienceEvent schema for offline purchase transactions, including fields for purchase amount, product SKU, and store location, and enable it for Real-Time Customer Profile with a customer identity descriptor.
t2: Prepare and upload a CSV or Parquet file containing historical offline purchase records to AEP using the batch ingestion API or the AEP UI, mapping each field to the corresponding XDM schema attribute.
t3: Confirm the batch dataset is enabled for Real-Time Customer Profile and monitor the ingestion job to completion, ensuring offline purchase history is merged into each customer's unified profile.

title: Exchange loyalty audience with retail co-marketing partner
t1: Build a loyalty program audience in Segment Builder by filtering on membership tier attributes and repeat purchase frequency over the past 90 days.
t2: Initiate a Segment Match connection by navigating to the Segment Match UI and sending a feed invitation to the retail co-marketing partner's AEP organization ID.
t3: Once the partner accepts the feed invitation, publish the loyalty audience to the Segment Match feed and confirm the overlap estimate before finalizing the share.

title: Receive and activate partner travel audience for upsell campaign
t1: Accept an inbound Segment Match feed invitation from a travel partner organization by reviewing the proposed connection in the Segment Match UI and approving it.
t2: Browse the shared feed to identify the partner-provided high-value traveler audience and add it to your AEP audience library by importing it into your sandbox.
t3: Use the imported partner audience as the entry condition in an AJO journey to trigger a personalized upsell email campaign for premium travel packages.

title: Validate audience overlap before data share with media agency
t1: Create a prospective customer audience in Segment Builder using CRM-derived identity attributes such as hashed email and phone number to ensure match compatibility with the media agency.
t2: Set up a Segment Match connection with the media agency's AEP organization and use the overlap preview report to evaluate the estimated identity match rate before committing to the share.
t3: After confirming a sufficient overlap threshold in the preview report, finalize the Segment Match feed configuration and publish the prospective customer audience for the media agency to activate in their campaigns.

title: Export audience segment memberships to Azure Blob Storage
t1: Navigate to the Destinations catalog and configure a new Azure Blob Storage destination by entering your storage account name, container name, and SAS token credentials.
t2: Select the audience membership dataset containing segment qualification records and map the identity namespace and segment membership fields to the corresponding Azure Blob destination schema.
t3: Activate the dataset export with a recurring daily schedule and specify the file format as Parquet so that audience membership snapshots are automatically delivered to your Azure container each day.

title: Stream experience event dataset to Amazon S3 for downstream analytics
t1: Set up an Amazon S3 destination in the Destinations catalog by providing your AWS access key, secret key, bucket name, and region to establish a secure connection.
t2: Choose the experience event dataset that captures behavioral clickstream data and configure the field mapping to align AEP event schema fields with the expected S3 output structure.
t3: Define an hourly incremental export schedule so that only newly ingested experience events are appended to the S3 bucket at each interval, reducing redundant data transfer.

title: Deliver B2B account dataset to SFTP for CRM synchronization
t1: Create a new SFTP destination in the Destinations catalog by supplying the hostname, port, username, and SSH key required to authenticate with your organization's SFTP server.
t2: Select the B2B account dataset and map key account attributes such as account ID, industry, and annual revenue to the column headers expected by the downstream CRM import process.
t3: Schedule a weekly full-file export to run every Monday morning so the CRM team receives a refreshed, complete snapshot of all B2B account records at the start of each business week.

title: Re-engage churned customers via Marketo email campaigns
t1: In Real-Time CDP, create a re-engagement audience by identifying profiles with no purchase activity in the last 90 days using behavioral event data and time-based segment rules.
t2: Configure the Marketo Engage destination connection in AEP, authenticating with Marketo API credentials and enabling field mapping between AEP profile attributes and Marketo person fields such as email, last purchase date, and customer tier.
t3: Activate the churned customer audience to the Marketo Engage destination so that matched contacts are automatically added to a dedicated win-back email program with personalized re-engagement messaging.

title: Suppress converted leads from Marketo prospecting programs
t1: In Real-Time CDP, define a suppression audience composed of profiles whose CRM opportunity stage has been updated to 'Closed Won' by ingesting Salesforce CRM data through a source connector and applying the appropriate segment filter.
t2: Add the Marketo Engage destination to the suppression audience and configure the segment membership mapping so that AEP communicates both audience entry and exit events to Marketo in real time.
t3: Activate the suppression audience to Marketo Engage so that newly converted customers are automatically removed from active prospecting and cold-outreach smart campaigns, preventing irrelevant communications.

title: Deliver product upsell audiences to Marketo for targeted outreach
t1: Use Real-Time CDP's computed attributes to calculate each customer's total lifetime value and product usage frequency, then build a high-value upsell audience targeting profiles that exceed defined LTV and engagement thresholds.
t2: Set up the Marketo Engage destination in AEP by providing the Munchkin account ID and OAuth credentials, then map computed attribute values such as LTV score and product tier to custom Marketo lead fields to enrich lead records upon activation.
t3: Activate the upsell audience to the Marketo Engage destination, triggering automatic enrollment of qualified leads into a Marketo upsell nurture program where sales representatives receive task alerts for high-priority follow-up.

title: Export Profile Data for Tableau Segmentation Analysis
t1: Use Query Service to write PSQL queries against the unified Profile store, extracting identity-stitched customer attributes and segment memberships into a derived dataset.
t2: Publish the derived dataset as a persistent Query Service table and connect Tableau to it via the PostgreSQL endpoint using time-based incremental refresh settings.
t3: Build a Tableau segment overlap matrix visualisation showing how customers qualify across multiple Real-Time CDP audiences simultaneously.

title: Analyse Journey Analytics Drop-off via Query Service and Tableau
t1: Query the ExperienceEvent dataset in Query Service to extract AJO journey step entry, progression, and exit events grouped by journey version ID and node name.
t2: Connect Tableau to the Query Service PostgreSQL endpoint and import the journey funnel result set, configuring a live connection to reflect near-real-time journey data.
t3: Design a Tableau funnel chart mapping each AJO journey node as a stage, highlighting drop-off rates and median time-between-steps to identify optimisation opportunities.

title: Visualise Consent and Data Governance Compliance Metrics in Tableau
t1: Write Query Service SQL to aggregate consent field values from the Profile union view, grouping opt-in and opt-out rates by marketing preference category, region, and data collection date.
t2: Schedule the Query Service query as a recurring job to refresh a persistent output dataset daily, then connect Tableau using PostgreSQL credentials pointing to that output table.
t3: Create a Tableau compliance dashboard displaying consent coverage percentage, opt-out trend lines, and geographic heat maps to support Data Governance reporting requirements.

title: Cross-Channel Attribution Reporting with Query Service and Tableau
t1: Use Query Service to join AJO message tracking datasets with ExperienceEvent conversion records, applying a last-touch attribution model in SQL across email, push, and SMS channels.
t2: Save the attribution output as a Query Service dataset view and authenticate Tableau Desktop against the Platform Query Service PostgreSQL endpoint to access the attributed results.
t3: Build a Tableau stacked bar chart breaking down revenue and conversion attribution by channel, campaign, and audience segment to guide budget allocation decisions.

title: Monitor Real-Time CDP Audience Refresh Latency via Tableau
t1: Query the segment membership and batch ingestion system datasets in Query Service to calculate the time delta between source data ingest completion and audience qualification update for each segment.
t2: Connect Tableau to Query Service via the PostgreSQL interface and pull the latency calculation results, setting the connection to refresh on a defined schedule aligned to batch cadence.
t3: Develop a Tableau operational monitoring dashboard with control charts showing average and peak audience refresh latency per segment, with threshold-based colour alerts for SLA breaches.

title: Lifetime Value Cohort Analysis Using Query Service and Tableau
t1: Author a Query Service SQL script that cohorts unified profiles by first-purchase month, then aggregates cumulative purchase value from ExperienceEvent commerce data to calculate 30, 60, and 90-day LTV per cohort.
t2: Persist the cohort LTV results in a Query Service output table and establish a Tableau connection using the Platform-provided PostgreSQL host, port, and credential set from the Queries UI.
t3: Construct a Tableau cohort retention heatmap where rows represent acquisition month cohorts and columns represent time periods, with cell colour intensity encoding cumulative lifetime value growth.

title: Monitor destination export failures with alerts
t1: Navigate to the Alerts section in Experience Platform and filter available alert types by the Destinations category.
t2: Subscribe to the destination dataflow run failure alert and configure SMS as the notification channel for your team.
t3: Receive an immediate SMS notification when a destination export dataflow fails, allowing you to investigate and retry the failed export before data gaps occur.

title: Track identity graph capacity thresholds with alerts
t1: Open the Alerts catalog in Experience Platform and search for identity-related alert types available for your sandbox.
t2: Subscribe to the identity graph capacity threshold alert and set email notifications to trigger when usage exceeds 90% of the allowed limit.
t3: Receive an email alert when identity graph usage approaches its limit, enabling your team to audit and deduplicate identity records before ingestion is blocked.

title: Alert on source connector ingestion delays
t1: Navigate to Alerts in Experience Platform and browse the Sources category to review available ingestion monitoring alert types.
t2: Subscribe to the sources dataflow run delay alert for a specific CRM source connector and configure in-platform notification delivery.
t3: Receive an in-platform notification when the CRM ingestion dataflow exceeds its expected run duration, prompting immediate investigation of upstream data pipeline bottlenecks.

title: Set up alerts for profile merge policy conflicts
t1: Access the Alerts section in Experience Platform and explore alert types related to Real-Time Customer Profile to identify merge policy conflict alerts.
t2: Enable the profile merge policy conflict alert and subscribe with your data engineering team email to ensure the right stakeholders are notified.
t3: Receive an email notification when a merge policy conflict is detected during profile unification, allowing your team to resolve conflicting rules and maintain data consistency.

title: Monitor journey publishing failures in AJO with alerts
t1: Navigate to the Alerts catalog in Experience Platform and filter for Journey Optimizer alert types related to journey execution and publishing.
t2: Subscribe to the journey publish failure alert and configure webhook-based notifications to integrate with your team's Slack channel.
t3: Receive a real-time Slack message when a journey fails to publish due to configuration errors, enabling the marketing team to quickly correct and redeploy the journey before campaign deadlines are missed.

title: Alert on query service compute hour overages
t1: Open the Alerts section in Experience Platform and locate alert types under the Query Service category to review available usage monitoring options.
t2: Subscribe to the query service compute hours threshold alert and set up email notifications to fire when 80% of the monthly compute allotment has been consumed.
t3: Receive a threshold warning email mid-month when compute usage is high, giving your analytics team time to optimize scheduled queries and avoid unexpected overage costs.

title: Re-engagement email with dynamic discount after cart abandonment
t1: Capture the cart abandonment event in Adobe Experience Platform by streaming real-time behavioral data when a customer leaves the site without completing purchase.
t2: Use AEP Computed Attributes to calculate the total cart value and determine the appropriate discount tier to offer the customer based on their historical spend profile.
t3: Trigger a Journey Optimizer email action using dynamic content blocks that render the exact abandoned products and the computed personalized discount code to incentivize checkout completion.

title: SMS follow-up sequence leveraging real-time customer segments
t1: Stream the cart abandonment Experience Event into AEP Real-Time Customer Profile to immediately update the customer's unified profile with the abandoned SKUs and session timestamp.
t2: Evaluate the updated profile against an AEP Streaming Segment that qualifies customers who have abandoned a cart containing high-margin products within the last two hours.
t3: Enroll qualified segment members in a Journey Optimizer SMS journey that delivers a time-sensitive text message with a direct deep-link back to the customer's saved cart.

title: In-app message retargeting using AI-driven next-best action
t1: Ingest cart abandonment behavioral signals from the mobile SDK into AEP and attach the event to the customer's Real-Time Customer Profile, including device context and product category.
t2: Invoke Adobe Journey Optimizer's AI-powered decisioning engine to select the next-best offer from the centralized offer library, ranked by predicted conversion probability for that customer.
t3: Deliver the winning offer as a personalized in-app message the next time the customer opens the mobile application, surfacing the relevant product imagery and offer details inline.

title: Paid media audience suppression and retargeting after abandonment
t1: Detect the cart abandonment event via AEP Web SDK data collection and flag the customer's profile with a propensity-to-abandon attribute using a pre-trained Adobe Sensei ML model.
t2: Activate the flagged customer segment from AEP to a paid media destination such as Google Display & Video 360, suppressing the customer from generic ads and enrolling them in a retargeting audience.
t3: Serve the customer dynamic product display ads featuring the exact items left in their cart, coordinated with a Journey Optimizer journey that caps ad frequency and aligns messaging with concurrent email touches.

title: Multi-step waitlist recovery journey with loyalty point incentive
t1: Listen for the cart abandonment Experience Event in Journey Optimizer using an event-triggered entry condition, capturing product IDs, quantities, and the customer's current loyalty tier from their Real-Time Profile.
t2: Apply a wait step of 24 hours within the Journey Optimizer canvas, then evaluate a re-entry condition to confirm the customer has still not completed purchase before proceeding to the incentive branch.
t3: Send a personalized email notifying the customer of a bonus loyalty points offer applied to their pending cart, using AJO's profile-based personalization to display their current points balance and the potential post-purchase total.

title: Cross-channel orchestration with consent-aware push and email fallback
t1: Receive the cart abandonment event in Journey Optimizer and look up the customer's Real-Time Profile to retrieve their current channel consent preferences stored in AEP's consent and preferences schema.
t2: Evaluate a consent-aware branching condition in the Journey Optimizer canvas: route customers who have opted into push notifications down the push channel path, and route all others to the email fallback path.
t3: Deliver a channel-appropriate message on each respective path — a rich push notification with product thumbnails for opted-in customers, or an HTML email with full cart details for those on the email path — ensuring full regulatory compliance.

title: Real-Time Customer Profile Enrichment and Segmentation
t1: Ingest behavioral and transactional data into AEP by enabling Profile and Identity stitching on ingested datasets.
t2: Define a computed attribute that aggregates purchase frequency and recency scores into the unified Real-Time Customer Profile.
t3: Build an audience segment in Audience Builder using the computed attribute thresholds to target high-value customers for downstream activation.

title: Cross-Channel Journey Orchestration with AJO
t1: Configure an AEP streaming source connector to capture real-time web clickstream events and map them to the XDM ExperienceEvent schema.
t2: Create a Journey trigger in Adobe Journey Optimizer using an audience qualification event so that customers entering the segment automatically enter the journey.
t3: Design a multi-step journey in AJO with conditional branches for email, push notification, and SMS channels based on customer engagement scores.

title: Data Governance and Policy Enforcement for Regulated Industries
t1: Apply DULE (Data Usage Labeling and Enforcement) labels to sensitive dataset fields such as health or financial identifiers within AEP Data Governance.
t2: Create custom data usage policies in AEP that restrict marketing activation for datasets carrying sensitive DULE labels.
t3: Activate a segment to an advertising destination and verify that AEP automatically blocks the activation and surfaces a policy violation alert.

title: B2B Account-Based Marketing with AEP and Marketo Integration
t1: Connect the Marketo Engage source connector to AEP to ingest B2B account, opportunity, and person records into XDM B2B schema classes.
t2: Build an account audience in AEP Real-Time CDP B2B Edition by filtering accounts with open opportunities above a defined revenue threshold.
t3: Activate the account audience to the LinkedIn Matched Audiences destination to serve targeted ads to buying committee members within those accounts.

title: Predictive Lead Scoring Using Customer AI
t1: Prepare and union historical conversion and behavioral datasets in AEP, ensuring they conform to the required Consumer ExperienceEvent and Individual Profile XDM schemas for AI model input.
t2: Configure and train a Customer AI instance by defining the propensity goal, prediction window, and eligible population, then run the scoring job to generate propensity scores.
t3: Use the output propensity score fields as segment filters in Segment Builder to create high-propensity audiences and route them into an AJO nurture journey.

title: Omnichannel Personalization with Adobe Target and AEP Edge Network
t1: Implement the AEP Web SDK on the brand website and configure a Datastream to route event data simultaneously to AEP, Analytics, and Adobe Target via the Edge Network.
t2: Create an AEP Edge segmentation rule that evaluates audience membership in milliseconds using streaming data so that segment status is available at the point of Target decisioning.
t3: Set up a Target A/B activity that uses AEP audience segments as targeting conditions to deliver personalized homepage hero content to qualifying visitors in real time.

title: Resolve Dataflow Backpressure by Adjusting Ingestion Batch Size
t1: Navigate to the Dataflows monitoring dashboard and identify a dataflow exhibiting consistently high processing latency and queue backpressure warnings.
t2: Drill into the dataflow's performance metrics to confirm that oversized batch payloads are exceeding the ingestion throughput threshold.
t3: Edit the source connector's advanced settings to reduce the batch size parameter and reschedule the dataflow run to validate improved throughput.

title: Recover a Paused Streaming Dataflow After Authentication Token Expiry
t1: Open the Sources monitoring view and locate a streaming dataflow showing a paused status with an authentication failure alert.
t2: Inspect the dataflow's error log to confirm the OAuth token used by the source connection has expired and is rejecting new data pushes.
t3: Update the source connection credentials with a refreshed OAuth token, then re-enable the streaming dataflow to restore continuous data flow.

title: Address Partial Record Ingestion Caused by Mandatory Field Violations
t1: Review the dataflow run summary in Sources monitoring and detect a high percentage of partial ingestion records flagged across recent runs.
t2: Open the failed records report to identify which mandatory XDM schema fields are missing from the incoming source payload.
t3: Update the field mapping in the dataflow transformation step to supply default values or derive the missing mandatory fields, then trigger a backfill run.

title: Diagnose and Fix Dataset Sink Failures Due to Capacity Limits
t1: Access the Dataflows monitoring panel and identify a dataflow with repeated sink-write failures targeting a specific Platform dataset.
t2: Examine the sink error details to confirm the target dataset has reached its storage quota, preventing new record writes from completing.
t3: Create a new target dataset with expanded capacity, reassign it as the dataflow sink in the connector configuration, and re-run the failed dataflow.

title: Restore a Scheduled Batch Dataflow Skipped Due to Dependency Conflicts
t1: In the Sources monitoring dashboard, identify a scheduled batch dataflow that was skipped during its last execution window without generating an error record.
t2: Review the dataflow execution timeline to discover that a concurrent overlapping run lock caused the scheduler to bypass the planned execution.

title: Real-Time Cart Abandonment Detection and Email Recovery
t1: AEP Real-Time Customer Data Platform detects cart abandonment event via streaming data ingestion when a user adds items to cart but does not complete checkout within 30 minutes, triggering a qualified segment update
t2: AJO Journey Orchestration receives the segment qualification signal and enrolls the customer into a cart abandonment journey, personalizing the message with abandoned product details, pricing, and customer loyalty tier data pulled from AEP unified profile
t3: AJO executes delivery of a personalized cart recovery email containing abandoned product images, a time-sensitive discount code, and a direct checkout link, with suppression logic applied for customers who completed purchase during journey wait period

title: Behavioral Scoring-Triggered SMS Cart Recovery Flow
t1: AEP Streaming Segmentation continuously evaluates user behavioral events including product views, add-to-cart, and session end signals to identify high-intent cart abandonment, computing a propensity score that crosses the abandonment threshold
t2: AJO Journey is triggered via API-triggered event sourced from AEP edge event forwarding, placing the customer into a multi-step wait logic that checks for purchase completion before advancing, and selects SMS as preferred channel based on AEP profile consent attributes
t3: AJO sends a personalized SMS recovery message referencing the specific abandoned product name and cart total, with a shortened trackable URL directing to a pre-populated cart, and logs delivery and click events back to AEP for experience event capture

title: High-Value Cart Abandonment with Push Notification Escalation
t1: AEP Data Collection captures mobile app events through the Edge Network SDK, identifying cart abandonment when a session timeout event fires after add-to-cart without a purchase event, and evaluates cart value against a high-value threshold segment rule
t2: AJO Journey Orchestration enrolls high-value cart abandoners into a priority recovery journey with condensed wait times, retrieves real-time inventory availability for abandoned items from AEP computed attributes, and prepares a personalized push notification payload
t3: AJO delivers an in-app push notification with dynamic content blocks showing the abandoned product image, remaining stock count to create urgency, and a one-tap deep link returning the customer directly to their active cart session

title: Omnichannel Cart Recovery with Channel Preference Optimization
t1: AEP Unified Profile aggregates cross-device behavioral signals and detects cart abandonment through a batch and streaming hybrid segment that identifies customers who have not returned to checkout within a configurable suppression window across web and mobile touchpoints
t2: AJO reads channel preference attributes and historical engagement data from the AEP profile to dynamically select the optimal recovery channel, routing customers into email, SMS, or push branches within the journey based on past open and click rate performance
t3: AJO dispatches the recovery message through the selected optimal channel with fully personalized content including product details, customer first name, and a channel-appropriate call to action, while writing journey interaction events back to AEP for downstream attribution modeling

title: Guest Shopper Cart Abandonment with Identity Resolution Recovery
t1: AEP Identity Service resolves a guest shopper's anonymous ECID to a known customer profile using email captured during cart entry, merging behavioral cart abandonment events with the authenticated profile to create a complete abandonment signal eligible for journey activation
t2: AJO Journey Orchestration is triggered by the identity-resolved profile entering the cart abandonment segment, applying business rules to exclude customers under global suppression or recent purchase conditions, and assembles personalized content using merged profile attributes
t3: AJO sends a recovery email addressed to the resolved customer identity containing their specific abandoned cart contents, personalized product recommendations based on AEP ML-driven affinity scores, and a loyalty points reminder to incentivize purchase completion

title: Time-Decay Multi-Touch Cart Abandonment Nurture Journey
t1: AEP Streaming Segmentation detects the initial cart abandonment event and creates a time-stamped segment membership entry, enabling AJO journey entry while also writing the abandonment event to the AEP data lake for downstream batch enrichment of customer lifetime value attributes
t2: AJO Journey applies a scheduled wait node and evaluates purchase completion status at multiple checkpoints, advancing non-converters through a sequence of escalating incentive messages while consuming updated AEP profile attributes at each decision node to ensure relevance
t3: AJO delivers a final high-incentive recovery message after the multi-touch sequence to persistently abandoned carts, including a personalized discount maximized for the customer's price sensitivity segment derived from AEP predictive attributes, with journey exit on purchase event receipt

title: AI-Powered Personalized Product Recommendation Cart Recovery
t1: AEP Customer AI scores each abandoning customer for purchase likelihood using historical behavioral features, and Streaming Segmentation flags profiles crossing a defined abandonment propensity threshold, enriching the profile with AI-generated next-best-action and recommended product attributes
t2: AJO Journey Orchestration consumes the AI-enriched AEP profile at journey entry to configure dynamic content slots, selecting between a direct cart recovery message for high-propensity customers and an alternative product suggestion message for lower-propensity customers likely to need alternative options
t3: AJO renders and delivers a personalized email or push notification combining the original abandoned cart items with AI-recommended complementary products sourced from AEP computed attributes, including social proof elements and a personalized subject line optimized through AJO content experimentation

title: B2B Cart Abandonment Journey with Account-Level Suppression
t1: AEP B2B Edition detects cart abandonment from an authenticated business buyer, enriching the person profile with account-level attributes including contract status, active sales engagement flags, and account tier, then evaluates whether the abandonment qualifies for marketing outreach versus sales handoff
t2: AJO Journey applies account-level suppression logic by checking AEP profile attributes for active opportunity flags, routing marketing-eligible abandoners into an email recovery branch while triggering a CRM task creation webhook for sales-engaged accounts, preventing channel conflict
t3: AJO delivers a business-appropriate cart recovery email to marketing-eligible B2B contacts referencing their organization name, abandoned product SKUs, and available volume pricing, with a meeting booking CTA embedded for high-value account tiers identified through AEP account profile data

title: Loyalty-Tiered Cart Abandonment Recovery with Dynamic Offers
t1: AEP Unified Profile captures cart abandonment behavioral events and enriches the signal with loyalty program attributes including tier status, available points balance, and tier upgrade proximity, feeding a composite abandonment segment that segments customers by loyalty engagement level
t2: AJO Journey Orchestration branches the recovery flow based on AEP loyalty tier attributes, configuring premium members for an exclusive early-access offer path, mid-tier members for a points-multiplier incentive path, and non-members for a first-purchase discount path with loyalty enrollment invitation
t3: AJO sends a tier-specific personalized recovery message through the customer's preferred channel, dynamically rendering the appropriate offer block, displaying current loyalty points balance and the points they would earn from completing the purchase, with real-time offer decisioning powered by AJO Offer Management

title: Cross-Device Cart Abandonment Unification and Recovery Sequence
t1: AEP Identity Graph stitches mobile and web behavioral events to detect a cross-device cart abandonment pattern where a customer added items on mobile but the session ended without purchase, with the desktop browsing session also failing to convert, creating a unified abandonment event on the merged profile
t2: AJO Journey receives the cross-device abandonment trigger with full context of the customer's multi-device journey, suppresses duplicate entry from secondary device signals, and retrieves the most recent cart snapshot from AEP experience events to construct an accurate and current recovery payload
t3: AJO delivers a cross-channel recovery communication that acknowledges the customer's multi-device browsing behavior with messaging referencing cart continuity across devices, providing a universal checkout link that works seamlessly on both mobile and desktop, and captures post-delivery engagement events back to AEP for journey analytics
